title: Kojima et al. 2024 (Dataset B) — Four-class ASME BCI: investigation of the feasibility and comparison of two strategies for multiclassing
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 15 healthy subjects performing an auditory brain-computer interface task based on the ASME (Auditory Stream segregation Multiclass ERP) paradigm. The study investigates two strategies for achieving four-class classification: ASME-4stream (four independent streams with single target stimuli) and ASME-2stream (two streams with dual target stimuli each). EEG data were acquired at 1000 Hz from 64 channels and analyzed using event-related potential methods and linear discriminant analysis classification, achieving accuracies of 83% and 86% respectively.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 1000 Hz from 64 channels using a BrainAmp system with standard 10-20 montage referenced to right mastoid. Subjects performed 12 runs alternating between ASME-4stream and ASME-2stream paradigms, each containing 4 trials of ~90s duration. ASME-4stream presented 4 auditory streams (SOA=150ms, 600 stimuli/trial, 9:1 standard:deviant ratio), while ASME-2stream presented 2 streams with 2 deviant stimuli each (SOA=300ms, 300 stimuli/trial, 8:1:1 ratio). Preprocessing included ICA-based artifact removal, bandpass filtering (1-40 Hz for ERP analysis, 0.1-8 Hz for classification), epoching (-0.1 to 1.2s), and downsampling to 250 Hz. Classification employed shrinkage-LDA with mean amplitudes from 10 non-overlapping intervals (0-1.0s) as features, evaluated using 4-fold chronological cross-validation.
